Episodes 1 to 11 of 18 are authored: 801 entities, 4,583 exact mentions in original-en and 4,623 in modern-en, 799 of the 801 bound in the older edition and 796 in the modern one, 116 focused tests passing, content revision 2026-09-16.11. NEXT: episode 12 (Cyclops, 566 paragraphs), Barney Kiernan's, the nameless narrator and the citizen. 3,159 paragraphs remain; the long ones are 15 (Circe, 1,441) and 17 (Ithaca, 654); episode 18 (Penelope) is eight paragraphs of monologue and will be the densest in the book.

THE RULE THAT GOVERNS THIS BOOK: A SURNAME IS ALMOST NEVER ONE MAN, SO KEY BY DEFAULT AND ALIAS ONLY ON PROOF. AND THE COROLLARY: RUN THE WHOLE-BOOK OCCURRENCE LIST ON EVERY ALIAS, NOT ONLY ON EVERY KEY. Four aliases have now been caught reaching past the episode that justified them -- PIPER into Peter Piper's tongue-twister at 9:117 (suppressed), LUCY into S. Lucy at 12:513 (keyed), JOHN MULLIGAN into 'Malachi Roland St John Mulligan' at 14:47 (keyed), and BOYD into 'that old fogey in Boyd's' at 11:102 (covered by a longer phrase). THE SWEEP THAT FINDS THEM: before authoring an episode, build the package and list every binding that already stands in it. That is how Boyd was found.

EPISODE 11 IS THE SOUND EPISODE AND ITS NAMES COME APART. Joyce fuses people into single words -- Bloowho, Bloowhose, Greaseabloom, Seabloom, Bloohimwhom, Siopold, Lionelleopold, Simonlionel, Bronzelydia, Minagold, Lidlydiawell, Bensoulbenjamin, Benaben, Benben, Kennygiggles, Bronzedouce, Blazure, Tomgin -- and splits them into two letters apiece: Lid Ker Cow De and Doll at 11:53 and 11:619. Each is bound by a PHRASE pattern, and a portmanteau that fuses two men is SPLIT BETWEEN THEM BY LOOKAROUND (Si(?=opold) to Simon, (?<=Si)opold to Bloom), the same technique Besteglinton needed in episode 9. THE MODERN EDITION UNDOES THREE OF THEM: Bloowhose becomes Bloom's at 11:120, greaseabloom becomes Greasy Bloom at 11:130, 11:134 and 11:628, and Bloohimwhom/Bloo becomes Bloom at 11:208. It also CAPITALISES JOYCE'S LOWERCASE 'miss' all through the episode, which is why Douce had to be added as a second alias, and it INTERPOLATES AN EDITORIAL GLOSS Joyce did not write -- 'Henry Flower (Bloom's pen name)' at 11:203 and 11:617. Those are the only two parentheses of their kind in the book; they are recorded as a source defect and are not bound.

NEW NAMESAKE SPLITS IN EPISODE 11, ALL KEYED: KENNEDY is the barmaid here but Peter Kennedy the hairdresser at 10:349 and James and Charles Kennedy the rectifiers at 10:435. MINA is Miss Kennedy here and Mina Purefoy everywhere else (8:86, 8:135, 14:49, 15:1235, 15:1340, 17:571, 18:0). PAT is bald Pat the Ormond waiter here and five other men elsewhere (3:59, 7:201 Pat Farrell, 8:35 Pat Claffey, 8:160 Pat Kinsella, 16:182 Pat Tobin). BEN is Ben Dollard except at 11:355 and 11:587, where Ben Howth is a hill. TOM is Tom Rochford at 11:283 and Tom Kernan at 11:483 and 11:627. GEORGE is George Lidwell except at 11:467, George Robert Mesias. LIONEL is the tenor of Flotow's Martha and also Lionel Marks the shopkeeper -- 11:617 has both, keyed by occurrence, and 11:621 is the shop alone. MARTHA is the opera's lost one and Martha Clifford, and 11:413 is both. PEAKE at 6:74 is a name in the deaths column and little Peake at 11:375 is Richie's companion at the old Royal. PLASTO at 4:25 and 6:82 is the legend in Bloom's hatband and at 11:467 the hatter himself. LAMBERT at 3:68 is Lambert Simnel; plain Lambert is Ned Lambert, and reading episode 11 turned up three paragraphs in EPISODE 10 that had been left unbound for want of the table -- 10:73, 10:186, 10:188.

ONE CARD WAS ABOUT TO BE DUPLICATED AND WAS CAUGHT BY THE BUILDER: THE BLIND STRIPLING OF EPISODE 8, whom Bloom takes across Dawson street, IS THE PIANO TUNER OF EPISODE 11 who left his tuningfork at the Ormond and taps back across the city for it. One card, extended. WHEN A LATER EPISODE NAMES SOMEBODY AN EARLIER ONE ONLY DESCRIBED, EXTEND THE EXISTING CARD. Miss Douce and Miss Kennedy were extended the same way and now carry their first names, Lydia and Mina.

DELIBERATELY UNBOUND IN EPISODE 11 AND RECORDED: BRONZE and GOLD, which name the two barmaids through the whole episode and are also colours -- binding either would put a card on half the chapter; BRONZELID at 11:601, which could be bronze-Lydia or bronze-Lidwell; LIDLYD at 11:35 and BLMSTUP and YRFMSTBYES at 11:559, which are past recovering; the croppy boy's MOTHER at 11:527 and his father and brothers at 11:533, and the TRAITOR SERVANT at 11:517, all inside the ballad; BY JOVE at 11:153, an oath; the shopfronts of the quays (Moulang's, Wine's, Carroll's, Cantwell's, Ceppi's, Bassi's, Graham Lemon's, Elvery's, Daly's, Barry's, Barney Kiernan's, Lionel Marks's, the Iveagh home, Keogh's) against AARON FIGATNER and PROSPER LORE, who ARE cast because the text attends to their names as men's names; the Collard grand, Cantrell and Cochrane's, number one Bass, Sceptre, Power (whiskey, not Jack Power), Goulding Collis Ward and Callan Coleman and Co (firms), Chickabiddy's owny Mumpsypum, and Bright's bright eye. ONE READING IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: 11:384, 'Wise child that knows her father, Dedalus said', is bound to SIMON, because the only Dedalus Bloom has spoken with today is the father.

A SILENT BINDER LIMITATION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY BOOK IN THIS LIBRARY: reviewed_aliases.py guards alias matches with \w, AND AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES \w, so an alias whose occurrence sits inside Gutenberg italics (_like this_) BINDS NOTHING AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. Four cases, all keyed: '_Los Demiurgos_' 3:1, '_Matcham's Masterstroke_' 4:162, '_That's not Mulcahy_' 6:325, '_Mr MacTrigger_' 8:208 and 8:223. The MacTrigger case was found by the omittedEntities line in the validation report and by nothing else -- READ THAT LINE ON EVERY BUILD. Over all 18 episodes the italic check also reports STEPHEN at 15:1133 (a stage direction, will need a key when Circe is read) and PATRICE at 16:212 (which is NOT Patrice Egan but 'the faubourg Saint Patrice' and will need suppressing).

A SECOND SILENT FAILURE, GUARDED: A REPEATED DICT LITERAL IN SPLIT OR PHRASE SHADOWS THE EARLIER ONE AND EVERY KEY IN IT CEASES TO EXIST. Tables.test_no_split_or_phrase_key_is_declared_twice parses the source and fails on any repeated key. NEVER RE-DECLARE A TABLE -- MERGE INTO THE EXISTING LITERAL. THE BUILD IS SLOW: about ten minutes of CPU for both editions, so run it in the background and wait on the log rather than polling. No edition byte was touched. This lane never sets appStatus.
